setup: Android 12 emulator, signed minified Release APKs. Identical 5,000-row list fixtures. Jump to the end and wait for its callback, then scroll through the middle for eight seconds at 600 pixels per second. Repeat before/after/after/before and after/before/before/after.
instrumentation:
from pathlib import Path
import shutil,sys
probe,source=map(Path,sys.argv[1:3])
target=probe/sys.argv[3]/'android'
shutil.copytree(source,target,dirs_exist_ok=True)
path=target/'app/src/main/java/dev/nexa/listobs/NexaGenerated.kt'
code=path.read_text()
needle='                    val nexaListState0 = rememberLazyListState()\n'
assert needle in code
code=code.replace(needle,needle+'''                    LaunchedEffect(nexaListState0) {
                        kotlinx.coroutines.delay(1800)
                        nexaListState0.scrollToItem(nexaListCount0 - 1)
                        kotlinx.coroutines.withTimeout(5000) {
                            while (nexa_hits == 0) kotlinx.coroutines.delay(10)
                        }
                        nexaListState0.scrollToItem(2500)
                        kotlinx.coroutines.delay(250)
                        val firstScans = nexaViewportChecks
                        val firstCpu = android.os.Process.getElapsedCpuTime()
                        val start = android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos()
                        var last = start
                        var callbacks = 0
                        nexaListState0.scroll {
                            while (last - start < 8_000_000_000L) {
                                androidx.compose.runtime.withFrameNanos { }
                                val now = android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos()
                                scrollBy(((now - last) * 0.0000006).toFloat())
                                last = now
                                callbacks++
                            }
                        }
                        android.util.Log.i("NexaListBench", org.json.JSONObject()
                            .put("watchChecks", nexaViewportChecks - firstScans)
                            .put("cpuMillis", android.os.Process.getElapsedCpuTime() - firstCpu)
                            .put("wallSeconds", (last - start) / 1e9)
                            .put("nativeFrameCallbacks", callbacks)
                            .put("lastItem", nexaListState0.firstVisibleItemIndex)
                            .put("endCallbacks", nexa_hits).toString())
                    }
''')
if 'snapshotFlow { run { val layoutInfo' in code:
    code=code.replace('snapshotFlow { run { val layoutInfo','snapshotFlow { nexaViewportChecks++; run { val layoutInfo',1)
else:
    needle='snapshotFlow {\n                                val layoutInfo'
    assert needle in code
    code=code.replace(needle,'snapshotFlow {\n                                nexaViewportChecks++\n                                val layoutInfo',1)
path.write_text(code+'\nprivate var nexaViewportChecks = 0\n')
limits: The probe counts end-predicate evaluations after the first callback. It measures process CPU and recent gfxinfo frames separately.

The baseline varies substantially in delivered frame cadence across emulator runs. These samples establish discontinued viewport work and preserved callback delivery, with overlapping CPU and frame timings.
